newsitem.title: POLAND: SBC WARBURG GIVES NFI UNITS "BUY" RATING.
newsitem.headline: SBC WARBURG GIVES NFI UNITS "BUY" RATING.

text.p: Investors should buy National Investment Fund (NFI) units, trading at about a 19-percent discount to book value, SBC Warburg in London said in its February 1997 report on the units.
The report said the units looked good compared to non-banks on the Warsaw bourse, which were trading at a p/bv of 1.9.

"If this ratio were to be applied to the book value of the (NFI units), the current price of 158 zlotys would represent a discount of 58 percent. Clearly this is optimistic but nevertheless illustrates the cheapness of the price," it said.
The units closed in regular bourse trade on Thursday at 149.5 zlotys.
SBC Warburg arrived at its book value for the NFI unit by adding the book values for all the funds which were published on June 30 of last year.
Under the government's mass privatisaton NFI programme, shares in some 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 funds run by foreign and domestic management firms.

The 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse in the second or third quarter of this year.
SBC Warburg said the recent announcement that the Bank of New York would create a US-dollar denominated Global Depositary Receipt (GDR) for the unit would greatly enhance trade by foreign investors.
It recommended investors to buy the unit at up to $80 through the newly created GDR.
It said the value of the units was further underpinned the the positive outlook for the Polish economy this year and by funds' corporate transactions such sales of firms at above book value.

SBC Warburg said the bourse's January rally and disappointing 1996 earnings for many companies made their valuations based on historic multiples look somewhat expensive, though hopes for better 1997 profits based on strong domestic demand and an expected EU recovery left some upside potential.
